import os, pathlib
wd='/home/ubuntu/continual-arc-baselines/.workbench/runs/adhoc-primeagentlearner-1790687629/attempts/1a23792c575c414fa559b68921d57662/system/state/workspace'
os.chdir(wd)
progdir=pathlib.Path(wd)/'programs'; progdir.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
p=progdir/'task-d58a1071.py'
code='''def transform(grid):
    g=[row[:] for row in grid]
    h,w=len(g),len(g[0])
    # Trace the short, one-cell-wide channel between two perpendicular walls.
    # The channel color is opposite the side-wall color; repaint its cells 4.
    candidates=[]
    for dr,dc in ((1,0),(0,1)):
        pr,pc=-dc,dr  # perpendicular unit vector
        for r in range(h):
            for c in range(w):
                v=g[r][c]
                if v not in (0,5):
                    continue
                rr,cc=r+pr,c+pc; r2,c2=r-pr,c-pc
                if not (0<=rr<h and 0<=cc<w and 0<=r2<h and 0<=c2<w):
                    continue
                wall=g[rr][cc]
                if wall not in (0,5) or wall==v or g[r2][c2]!=wall:
                    continue
                # Walk the contiguous channel cells with the same side walls.
                if r-dr>=0 and r-dr<h and c-dc>=0 and c-dc<w:
                    prev=(r-dr,c-dc)
                    if g[prev[0]][prev[1]]==v and all(0<=prev[0]+s*pr<h and 0<=prev[1]+s*pc<w and g[prev[0]+s*pr][prev[1]+s*pc]==wall for s in (-1,1)):
                        continue
                cells=[]; x,y=r,c
                while (0<=x<h and 0<=y<w and g[x][y]==v and
                       0<=x+pr<h and 0<=y+pc<w and 0<=x-pr<h and 0<=y-pc<w and
                       g[x+pr][y+pc]==wall and g[x-pr][y-pc]==wall):
                    cells.append((x,y)); x+=dr; y+=dc
                if not (2<=len(cells)<=5):
                    continue
                # At least one end is capped by the wall color, rather than
                # simply being an unbounded edge of the larger background line.
                before=(cells[0][0]-dr,cells[0][1]-dc)
                after=(cells[-1][0]+dr,cells[-1][1]+dc)
                capped=False
                for a,b in (before,after):
                    if 0<=a<h and 0<=b<w and g[a][b]==wall:
                        capped=True
                if capped:
                    candidates.append((len(cells),cells,v))
    if candidates:
        # The task marks the short enclosed channel, not the long boundary strokes.
        _,cells,_=min(candidates,key=lambda z:z[0])
        for r,c in cells:
            g[r][c]=4
    return g
'''
p.write_text(code)
print(p)
exec(compile(code,str(p),'exec'),globals())
